references.text: Pharaoh responds to Moses' original request to travel three days into the wilderness to sacrifice to the Lord.
Moses and Aaron first ask Pharaoh to let the people go into the wilderness to hold a feast for the Lord.
Pharaoh asks Moses to intercede during the plague of frogs, just as he does here during the plague of flies.
Moses intercedes for Pharaoh in response to this request.
Pharaoh again asks Moses to intercede during the plague of hail, a repeated pattern of temporary concessions.
Pharaoh once more asks for intercession during the plague of locusts, showing his pattern of false promises.
Pharaoh continues to set conditions on Israel's departure, just as he here limits how far they may go.
Job is asked to intercede for his friends, similar to Moses' role as an intercessor for Pharaoh.
Traces the development of negotiations from the original demand to Pharaoh's first attempt at compromise.
Contrasts God's unchanging requirement with Pharaoh's compromised response.
Highlights the contrast between God's demand for complete freedom and Pharaoh's limited permission.
Reminds of the original message that Pharaoh now tries to alter the terms of.
Contrasts Pharaoh's attempt at control with God's prophesied total liberation.
